title: Aside on name spellings, Elton John's movie and Sportin' Life
summary: A tangent about Rubinstein and Stein spellings, Elton John's movie and Gershwin's Porgy and Bess.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: By the way, Rubenstein, no, what does he say, Rubenstein, or Rubenstien? I get so confused these days.
It's Stein anyway.
I know it's Stein, but most New York Jews seem to change the .....
I call everybody Stein that's got EI.
And here they seem to make the EI an IE sound.
George (Jerry Wein) calls himself George (Jerry) Wien right?
He spells it Wein, I don't know why it isn't Wein.
(LAUGHTER).
Well anyway, Rubenstein, his son, John, who is an actor.
An actor, yes, right.
Yes, in 'Pippin'
He was in some movie with Elton John.
Oh was he?
Yes. Did you see that movie? That cowboy movie that Elton John was in?
No.
What was that called now? That one was great. And as soon as Elton he was killed, the picture was.................... It was that kind of thing too................................
Now I've forgotten what I was going to say. (LAUGHTER).
It was about Rubenstein.
Oh dear!
I was talking about Gershwin.
Oh yes I know, you mentioned Porgie and Bess. And he said his dream is to play
Sportin' Life
